subject: Passing reactive inputs to a module

messages.author: a6f35117e675c51c
messages.subject: Passing reactive inputs to a module
parts:
In the documentation of modules it mentions that if a module wants to have access to an input that is not part of a module you have to explicitly pass it.
callModule(myModule, "myModule1", reactive(input$checkbox1))

Can someone give me a use case of this. a small dummy code will do just fine.

messages.author: eed50af6f634e08b
messages.subject: Re: Passing reactive inputs to a module
parts:
You would simply do something like this when defining the module:

myModule <- function(input, output, session, input) {
print(isolate(input()))

}

messages.author: a6f35117e675c51c
messages.subject: Re: Passing reactive inputs to a module
parts:
So you cannot actually pass variables between sibling modules, nor with child parent module. You can only pass variables that are not part of any module to the module
passing variables between sibling as to be explicit. The sibling server code should return the input required by it's sibling or parent.

messages.author: eed50af6f634e08b
messages.subject: Re: Passing reactive inputs to a module
parts: Yes you can. You can return an object in a module (which may be a list of reactive objects and thus also inputs), and use it somewhere else. This is clearly described in the article on Shiny modules here: http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/modules.html.
